# Flex IOT server: integration guide for AI assistants building a mobile app

> Flex IOT lets a user register IoT devices (switches, sensors, ...), group them into rooms, pair them
> with a one-time code, and see/control them live over MQTT. This file tells you how to build the
> Android or iOS client for it. Follow it literally; do not invent endpoints.

BASE = the server URL you were given, e.g. https://iot.example.com (always https). All paths below are
relative to BASE. All bodies and responses are JSON. Users never see or need to know about Hive or
blockchain: they sign in with Google or email through "Snapie" and that is all.

## 1. Architecture in one minute
- REST API under BASE/api for accounts, devices, rooms, pairing.
- MQTT broker for live data. The app connects with MQTT over secure WebSocket (wss) using short-lived
  credentials from the API. The app only reads its own topics and only publishes commands.
- Physical devices pair separately (section 6) and publish state; the app never sees their passwords.

## 2. Sign in (do this exactly)
Login uses Snapie's web login page in the system browser plus PKCE. The app never handles passwords.

1. Generate `verifier`: 43 to 128 chars from [A-Za-z0-9_-] (32 random bytes, base64url, no padding).
   Keep it in memory (or secure storage) until step 5.
2. `challenge = base64url_no_padding(SHA256(verifier))` (always 43 chars).
3. `GET /api/auth/start?platform=app&challenge=<challenge>` -> `{"state": "...", "url": "https://.../login?..."}`.
4. Open `url` in the system auth browser (see platform notes). The user signs in there. When done the
   browser navigates to the app's registered redirect:
   `<app-scheme>://auth?token=<snapie-token>&state=<state>`  or on failure  `...?error=<code>&state=<state>`.
   Check that `state` equals the one from step 3 before continuing.
5. Immediately (the token lives 120 seconds): `POST /api/auth/snapie` with
   `{"token": "<snapie-token>", "state": "<state>", "verifier": "<verifier>"}`
   -> `{"token": "<session>", "user": "<user id>", "name": "<display name or null>", "admin": false}`.
   `state` is single use: if this call fails, restart from step 1.
6. Store `token` in secure storage (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore-backed storage). Send it on every
   API call as `Authorization: Bearer <session>`. It is valid 7 days; there is no refresh: on any 401
   run the sign-in again.
7. Sign out: `POST /api/auth/logout` (Bearer, body `{}`), then delete the stored token.

`GET /api/me` (Bearer) -> `{"user", "name", "admin"}`. Show `name` in the UI so users can see who they
are signed in as. There is no email available; do not ask Snapie for one.

The redirect scheme is fixed by the server (`APP_REDIRECT`, default `menoiot://auth`) and must also be
registered on the Snapie side. If you change the app's URL scheme, the server owner must update both;
otherwise login ends on a Snapie error page.

## 3. Platform differences (read this)
iOS
- Use `ASWebAuthenticationSession` with `callbackURLScheme` = the scheme (e.g. `menoiot`). Do NOT use
  WKWebView or SFSafariViewController. No Info.plist URL scheme entry is needed for this API.
- Keep the session token in the Keychain.
- App Store rule 4.8: an app that offers a third-party social login (Google) must also offer an
  equivalent privacy-preserving option, i.e. Sign in with Apple. SIGN IN WITH APPLE IS NOT AVAILABLE
  through this login flow today (the Snapie login page offers Google and email only). Treat it as a
  required follow-up before App Store submission; see section 9. Do not fake it client-side.
- iOS suspends network sockets shortly after the app goes to the background; the MQTT connection will
  drop. Reconnect on foreground and reload state. There is no push notification support yet.
- Trusted TLS certificates only (Let's Encrypt is fine). Self-signed certificates will fail.

Android
- Use Chrome Custom Tabs (`androidx.browser`) or AppAuth / `flutter_web_auth_2`. Do NOT use an embedded
  WebView: Google refuses sign-in inside WebViews.
- Declare the redirect as an intent filter on the receiving activity: action VIEW, categories DEFAULT
  and BROWSABLE, `<data android:scheme="menoiot" android:host="auth"/>`. Use `launchMode="singleTask"`
  so the result returns to the running activity.
- Keep the session token in EncryptedSharedPreferences / Keystore.
- Doze and background limits stop idle sockets; reconnect when the app returns to the foreground.
  Real-time background alerts would need FCM, which this server does not provide yet.
- Cleartext HTTP is blocked by default; everything here is https/wss so no network config is needed.

Both: other apps can claim the same custom scheme. PKCE (step 2) is what makes a hijacked redirect
useless, so never skip the verifier.

## 4. REST API (all except /api/auth/*, /api/pair need Bearer)
Content-Type must be application/json on any POST/PATCH/PUT, even with an empty body (send `{}`).
Errors are `{"error": "<code>"}`: 400 invalid_*/bad_request, 401 unauthorized, 403 admin_required,
404 not_found, 415 json_required, 429 rate limited (back off and retry).

GET  /api/me
GET  /api/types -> [{key, name, category, schema}]   device types; schema = {state:{...}, cmd:{...}}
GET  /api/rooms -> [{id, name}]
POST /api/rooms {name} -> {id, name}                 name 1-64 chars, max 50 rooms per user
PATCH /api/rooms/:id {name}
DELETE /api/rooms/:id                                devices in it are kept, just unassigned
GET  /api/devices -> [{id, name, type, room, paired, created, topic}]   room = room id or null
POST /api/devices {name, type, room?} -> {id, name, type, room, topic, pairing:{code, expiresIn}}
PATCH /api/devices/:id {name?, room?}                room:null removes it from its room
DELETE /api/devices/:id                              also revokes the device's credentials
POST /api/devices/:id/pairing-code -> {code, expiresIn}   new one-time code (invalidates the old one)
POST /api/mqtt-token {} -> {url, username, password, topic, expiresIn}

Build the device-type picker from GET /api/types (the list changes without app updates). Render by
`category`: `switch` -> toggle, `sensor` -> value + unit. For an unknown category show the raw state
JSON; never crash.

## 5. Live data over MQTT
1. `POST /api/mqtt-token` -> `{url: "wss://host/mqtt", username, password, topic: "u/<user>/#", expiresIn: 3600}`.
2. Connect an MQTT 3.1.1 client over WebSocket to `url` with that username/password. Use a unique
   clientId. Subscribe to `topic`.
3. Credentials last `expiresIn` seconds (1 hour). Before that, fetch a new token and reconnect;
   after expiry the broker denies everything. Never cache the password to disk.

Topics (every device has `topic` from the REST API, call it T = `u/<user>/d/<device_id>`):
- `T/state`  JSON from the device, shaped by its type schema, e.g. switch `{"on":true}`, sensor
  `{"value":21.5,"unit":"C"}`. Treat fields as optional.
- `T/status` plain text `online` or `offline`.
- `T/cmd`    the ONLY topic the app may publish to. JSON per the type's `cmd` schema, e.g.
  `{"on":true}`. Publish with QoS 0 or 1, retain = false.
The ACL denies anything else, including other users' topics. There is no wildcard publish.

Rooms are only labels in the API. They are not in topic names, so moving a device between rooms
never changes its topic. For "all lights off" in a room, publish one `cmd` per device in it.

## 6. Adding a device from the app
1. `POST /api/devices {name, type, room?}` -> read `pairing.code` (8 chars, valid 10 minutes, single
   use). Show it to the user or hand it to the device (BLE / Wi-Fi provisioning).
2. The DEVICE (not the app) calls `POST /api/pair {"code": "ABCD2345"}` (no auth, rate limited) and gets
   `{host, port, tls, username, password, clientId, publish:{state,status}, subscribe:{cmd}}`, then
   connects to the broker over TLS on `port` and uses exactly those topics.
3. The device appears with `paired: true` in `GET /api/devices` and `online` once it connects.
Re-pairing (new code) replaces the device password; the old password stops working for new connections.

## 7. Suggested screens
Sign in; device list grouped by room (name, online badge, value, toggle); add device (name, type,
room) -> pairing code screen; device detail (rename, move room, new pairing code, delete); settings
(signed-in name, sign out). Reload `GET /api/devices` after any change; apply live changes from MQTT.

## 8. Do not
- Do not embed API keys or the broker secret; there are none for clients.
- Do not call endpoints starting with `/broker/`; they are internal.
- Do not store the Snapie token or verifier after step 5; keep only the session token.
- Do not poll REST for state; use MQTT.

## 9. Known gaps (do not pretend these exist)
- Sign in with Apple: not offered by the login page used here. Needed for App Store review if Google
  login is shown (see iOS notes). The server owner must add it on the Snapie side first.
- Push notifications for background alerts: not implemented (no APNs/FCM).
- Telemetry history and charts: not implemented; only the latest state is available live.
- Token refresh: none; sign in again after 7 days.
